graph_theory.title: Wagner's theorem on planar graphs (1937)
graph_theory.description: Wagner proved a graph is planar iff it contains neither K5 nor K3,3 as a minor. Refinement of Kuratowski's earlier subdivision-based theorem. Method: structural induction; case analysis on minor-closed properties; characterization via excluded minors. Established the excluded-minor framework that Robertson-Seymour later generalized.

graph_theory.title: Hadwiger's conjecture and partial results (1943-present)
graph_theory.description: Conjecture: every graph with chromatic number k contains K_k as a minor. Partial results: k=4 by Wagner; k=5 by Robertson-Seymour-Thomas (1993, equivalent to 4CT). Higher k open. Methodology: structural decomposition; reduction to extremal cases; using minor-closed properties; flag bounds via probabilistic arguments and graph minor structure theorem.

graph_theory.title: Tutte's reformulation and partial proof attempts on 4CT (1946-1976)
graph_theory.description: Tutte studied 4-coloring via dual chromatic polynomial, edge-colorings of cubic graphs, and snark constructions (cubic graphs not 3-edge-colorable). Showed 4CT equivalent to Tait's conjecture: every cubic bridgeless planar graph is 3-edge-colorable. Methodology: dual reformulation; combinatorial counting; constructive case analysis; identifying obstructions (snarks).

graph_theory.title: Max-flow min-cut theorem (Ford-Fulkerson, 1956)
graph_theory.description: Ford-Fulkerson: maximum flow value equals minimum cut capacity in any flow network. Algorithm: augmenting paths; integer capacities yield integer max-flow; LP duality interpretation. Applications: bipartite matching (König), edge connectivity (Menger), system of distinct representatives (Hall). Methodology: duality between primal and dual problems; iterative refinement via augmenting paths; structural characterization.

graph_theory.title: Halin's grid theorem (1965)
graph_theory.description: Every infinite locally-finite graph contains either an infinite ray or an infinite-degree vertex. Strengthening: every infinite graph with no two disjoint infinite paths has bounded tree-width. Methodology: extremal infinite combinatorics; tree decomposition; König's lemma applications; structural characterization by exclusion of canonical objects.

graph_theory.title: Erdős-Ko-Rado theorem (1961)
graph_theory.description: Maximum size of a family of k-element subsets of {1..n} with pairwise non-empty intersection is C(n-1, k-1). Method: shifting / compression — replace family with a more structured equivalent; cyclic counting argument. Methodology: extremal set theory; compression operator (replace pair (i,j) with (i,i'))  with i' < j; structural reduction via canonical form.

graph_theory.title: Karchmer-Wigderson theorem on circuit depth (1990)
graph_theory.description: Communication complexity of relation R(f) equals depth of optimal Boolean circuit computing f. Reduces circuit lower bounds to communication complexity lower bounds. Method: bidirectional translation between circuit structure and protocol structure; protocol-tree-to-circuit construction and inverse. Methodology: cross-domain equivalence (circuits ↔ protocols); structural correspondence; leveraging communication-complexity tools for circuit bounds.

graph_theory.title: Menger's theorem on graph connectivity (1927)
graph_theory.description: In any graph, the maximum number of vertex-disjoint paths between u and v equals the minimum number of vertices whose removal separates u from v. Generalization: edge version (Ford-Fulkerson). Method: induction on graph size; augmenting path argument; LP duality interpretation. Methodology: max-min duality theorem; vertex/edge cut equivalence; structural characterization.

complexity_theory.title: Karp's 21 NP-complete problems (1972)
complexity_theory.description: Karp showed 21 natural combinatorial problems (knapsack, vertex cover, set cover, Hamiltonian cycle, graph coloring, etc.) are NP-complete via polynomial-time reductions from SAT. Founded the catalog of NP-complete problems. Method: explicit reduction from SAT or another known NPC problem; preserving solution structure; verifying reduction is polynomial-time. Methodology: chain of reductions starting from Cook-Levin; constructing problem-to-problem encodings.

complexity_theory.title: Razborov's monotone circuit lower bound (1985)
complexity_theory.description: Razborov proved cliques have super-polynomial monotone circuit complexity, breaking the long-standing barrier on non-trivial circuit lower bounds. Method: approximation by simpler functions; counting argument over approximations; structural decomposition into compatible modules. Methodology: replace function by a class of approximating functions, count how many monotone circuits could approximate, derive contradiction from counting.

complexity_theory.title: Yao's minimax principle (1977)
complexity_theory.description: Yao showed expected complexity of best randomized algorithm against worst-case input equals worst-case complexity of best deterministic algorithm against worst-case input distribution. Application: lower bounds via choosing hard distribution. Method: minimax theorem from game theory applied to algorithm-vs-input games; LP duality. Methodology: game-theoretic framing; minimax theorem; reduction to deterministic lower bound under structured distribution.

complexity_theory.title: IP = PSPACE (Lund-Fortnow-Karloff-Nisan + Shamir, 1990)
complexity_theory.description: Interactive proof systems with polynomial verifier and unbounded prover decide exactly PSPACE. Method: arithmetization of Boolean formulas (replace with low-degree polynomials over a field); sumcheck protocol; recursive interactive verification. Methodology: arithmetization technique (compute Boolean things via polynomial extension); recursive protocol construction; verifier-prover dance with polynomial check at each round.

complexity_theory.title: PCP theorem (Arora-Lund-Motwani-Sudan-Szegedy + Arora-Safra, 1992)
complexity_theory.description: NP problems have probabilistically-checkable proofs of polynomial length verifiable by reading O(1) bits. Implies hardness of approximation for many problems. Method: error-correcting codes as proof structure; recursive composition of low-degree-test verifiers; gap amplification via parallel repetition. Methodology: encode proofs in highly redundant form; verification via local tests; gap amplification through composition.

complexity_theory.title: Toda's theorem (1989): PH ⊆ P^#P
complexity_theory.description: Toda proved the polynomial hierarchy is contained in P with #P oracle. Implies counting is at least as hard as the entire polynomial hierarchy. Method: probabilistic XOR-clauses; isolation lemma (Mulmuley-Vazirani); reduction from PH to #SAT-counting. Methodology: probabilistic technique to isolate solutions; counting reduction; structural decomposition of PH levels.

complexity_theory.title: Levin's universal search (1973)
complexity_theory.description: Levin defined universal search: enumerate all algorithms by description length and run them in parallel with time-budget proportional to 2^(-description-length). For any algorithm A solving a problem in time t(n), universal search solves it in time O(2^|A| · t(n)). Method: dovetailing across algorithms; meta-level optimization; description-length-weighted scheduling. Methodology: enumerate-and-test at meta-level; optimal up-to-constant within search class.

complexity_theory.title: Valiant's holographic algorithms (2002-2008)
complexity_theory.description: Valiant introduced holographic algorithms: solve combinatorial counting problems via Pfaffian/perfect-matching reductions and tensor manipulation. Method: encode problem as tensor contraction; find a basis change such that tensor becomes Pfaffian-evaluable; reduce to perfect-matching counting in planar graph. Methodology: tensor reformulation; basis change via change-of-coordinates in tensor space; reduction to known-tractable problem class.

geometric_flow_pde.title: Hamilton's mean curvature flow (1982)
geometric_flow_pde.description: Mean curvature flow: surface evolves by velocity equal to mean curvature vector. Hamilton showed for closed convex hypersurfaces, the flow contracts to a round point (preserving relative shape under rescaling). Methodology: PDE techniques on geometric quantities; Harnack inequalities; preserved geometric inequalities via maximum principle; barrier comparisons; ODE comparison for ODEs derived from PDE invariants.

geometric_flow_pde.title: Yang-Mills heat flow (Donaldson, Atiyah-Bott)
geometric_flow_pde.description: Heat flow on space of connections in a principal bundle; gradient flow of Yang-Mills functional. Donaldson used to study moduli space of self-dual connections on 4-manifolds, leading to Donaldson invariants distinguishing smooth structures on 4-manifolds. Method: gradient flow on infinite-dimensional manifold; convergence to critical points; analyzing limit configurations as moduli structure. Methodology: gradient-flow construction; bubbling/concentration analysis; moduli-space compactification.

geometric_flow_pde.title: Harmonic map heat flow (Eells-Sampson, 1964)
geometric_flow_pde.description: Harmonic map flow: gradient flow of energy functional on space of maps between Riemannian manifolds. Eells-Sampson: when target has non-positive curvature, flow converges to harmonic map. Method: parabolic PDE techniques; energy estimates; non-positive-curvature monotonicity. Methodology: gradient flow; energy functional monotonicity; structural assumption on target geometry; long-time existence + convergence.

geometric_flow_pde.title: Schoen-Yau positive mass theorem (1979)
geometric_flow_pde.description: Schoen-Yau: in general relativity, the total mass of an isolated gravitational system is non-negative, and zero iff system is Minkowski. Method: spinors-free proof using minimal surface theory; analyzing area-minimizing surfaces in asymptotically-flat manifolds. Methodology: minimal surface analysis; structure of stable minimal surfaces; reduction to lower-dimensional case; combining geometric estimates.

geometric_flow_pde.title: Brendle's classification of 3-dim Type-I Ricci-flow singularities (2018)
geometric_flow_pde.description: Brendle classified Type-I Ricci-flow singularity models in 3D under non-negative curvature. Method: tangent flow analysis; rigidity statements about ancient solutions; pinching estimates; reduction to model space comparison. Methodology: classify singularity types via blowup analysis; rigidity under symmetry assumption; structural classification of solitons.

geometric_flow_pde.title: Calibrated geometry (Harvey-Lawson, 1982)
geometric_flow_pde.description: Harvey-Lawson introduced calibrations: closed forms whose pullback to any submanifold is at most the volume form, with equality on calibrated submanifolds. Calibrated submanifolds are automatically area-minimizing. Examples: Kähler, special Lagrangian, associative, Cayley. Method: differential-form construction; comparison principle; structure theorems on calibrated submanifolds. Methodology: identify a closed form satisfying comparison inequality; characterize equality case as canonical class.

geometric_flow_pde.title: De Giorgi's regularity theorem (1957)
geometric_flow_pde.description: De Giorgi proved minimizers of elliptic functionals are Hölder continuous. Resolved Hilbert's 19th problem on regularity of variational solutions. Method: oscillation decay across nested balls; iterative integral inequality; Moser iteration. Methodology: prove uniform decay in finer scales; iterative L^∞ to L^p estimate; structural reduction to scale-invariant inequality.

geometric_flow_pde.title: Moser's Harnack inequality (1961)
geometric_flow_pde.description: Moser proved: positive solutions to elliptic divergence-form equations satisfy Harnack inequality (sup_K u ≤ C · inf_K u for any compact K). Generalizes classical Harnack from harmonic functions to a wide class of operators. Method: iterative L^p bounds; John-Nirenberg lemma; integration by parts; Caccioppoli inequalities. Methodology: chain of L^p estimates; iteration scheme converting L^p control to L^∞ control; structural inequality at each scale.
